lines.text: My dad's old answering machine still sits on our kitchen counter... three years after his funeral.
Mom won't let anyone touch it. And she has one rule.
If that little red light is ever blinking... don't listen. Just erase it.
I thought it was grief. Nobody even calls that number anymore.
Then, one morning in December, I came down for breakfast... and the light was blinking.
Mom was still asleep. And I missed him so much.
Static. A long, tired breath. And then my dad's voice, low and shaking.
Don't let your mother go down to the basement tonight. No matter what she hears.
That night, I woke up at three a.m. to the basement door... creaking open.
I told myself it was a dream. I pulled the blanket over my head... and I didn't get up.
In the morning, Mom was at the stove, humming... like nothing ever happened.
And the red light was blinking again.
It was Mom's voice this time. Whispering. Honey... it's so dark down here. Who's in the kitchen with you?
